newsitem.title: LATVIA: ECONOMY MINISTRY SEES 4 PCT 1997 GROWTH.
newsitem.headline: ECONOMY MINISTRY SEES 4 PCT 1997 GROWTH.

text.p: Latvian Economy Minister Guntar Krasts said on Thursday that he expected the economy to grow around four percent this year.
Citing a biannual report on the economy by the ministry, he also predicted inflation of around 10 percent this year and a slight rise in unemployment to 7.6 percent.
"GDP in 1997 could reach around four percent annual growth," Krasts told a news conference.
"That is not enough but our forecasts try to be realistic," he added.
He said that output and GDP growth would spread into all branches of the economy, making the base for growth wider than in just separate sectors as last year.
A longer-term strategy of economic development is planned to be submitted to the parliament together with the draft budget later this year, Krasts said.
"This strategy, a couple years overdue, is one of the main tasks ofthe ministry to secure further stable growth trend," Krasts said.
